A gap assessment can identify what is missing. It cannot decide who will close it.

That is where preparation work often slows down. A finding needs more than a label. It needs an accountable owner, the authority to make the change, known dependencies, a target date, and a clear definition of completion.

We at Cloud2e connect CMMC gap assessment to remediation planning and documentation work, including SSP and POA&M support. The intended benefit is to turn a list of findings into work the technical and business teams can actually manage.

A useful Sunday question: if you opened your readiness plan today, could you name the owner and next action for every open gap? If not, start with the highest-impact items and assign responsibility before adding another tool or spreadsheet.

Preparation moves when ownership is visible.

A gap without an owner is a future meeting topic, not a remediation plan.

After a CMMC gap assessment, each finding should be translated into an executable work item:

• named owner
• decision authority
• required resources and dependencies
• target completion date
• evidence to retain
• acceptance criteria for closure

Cloud2e’s CMMC preparation services include gap assessment, remediation support, SSP and POA&M work, and documentation organization. Connecting those activities helps teams move from identifying weaknesses to managing the work required to address them.

The goal is not to create the longest findings register. It is to build a readiness plan that technical leads, leadership, and compliance stakeholders can understand and operate together.
